heroLead: Carbon Hill's name says everything about its history, a Walker County coal town built directly on top of the seams that later became coalbed methane targets in the Black Warrior Basin.
intro: Coal mining defined Carbon Hill from its founding, and land here was routinely acquired or leased with the mineral estate separated from the surface, a pattern that made later coalbed methane leasing straightforward for operators but often left individual families unclear about exactly what they still owned. We buy those mineral interests directly, and this page covers how we approach Carbon Hill-area ownership and value.

Because so much of the original acreage here was acquired in large blocks, a current owner's share is often quite small, sometimes a sixteenth or less of what a great-grandparent originally held. We buy at that scale once ownership is confirmed.

sections.heading: A coal town's layered mineral title
paragraphs: Given how thoroughly coal companies acquired mineral rights around Carbon Hill in the early 1900s, tracing a current owner's interest often means following a chain through a former mining company, its later corporate successors, and eventually a sale or inheritance back into private hands. That chain matters for confirming what a present-day heir actually holds.

sections.heading: Walker County's place in the CBM play
paragraphs: Walker County sits on the northern side of the Black Warrior Basin's coalbed methane fairway, with activity historically lighter than the Brookwood-Oak Grove core farther south in Tuscaloosa County. We check current permit and well records for the specific area around a Carbon Hill tract before offering any range.

sections.heading: Confirming ownership through county records
paragraphs: Walker County's courthouse in Jasper holds the deed and probate history needed to trace most Carbon Hill-area mineral interests. We pull that record as part of every offer, particularly for older reservations that predate any current owner's direct memory of the transaction.

faqs.question: Our land near Carbon Hill has an old coal company reservation. Do we still own anything?
faqs.answer: Possibly, depending on how the chain of title developed since. We trace the reservation through its corporate history and any later transfers to confirm what your family currently holds.

faqs.question: Is there active coalbed methane drilling right around Carbon Hill?
faqs.answer: Walker County has seen less dense CBM activity than the Brookwood-Oak Grove core to the south, so we check current records for your specific parcel before quoting.

faqs.question: What records do you need to confirm ownership here?
faqs.answer: A deed, will, or probate record is most useful, but if you don't have one, we can search Walker County's courthouse records in Jasper to help trace it.

faqs.question: My share is small, maybe a sixteenth or less. Is it worth selling?
faqs.answer: Yes, we regularly buy interests at that scale once your exact percentage is confirmed against county records.
